newsitem.title: USA: Farmland says Q3 earnings up 22 pct vs year-ago.
newsitem.headline: Farmland says Q3 earnings up 22 pct vs year-ago.

text.p: Farmland Industries Inc said Monday that net income in the fiscal 1997 third quarter rose 22 percent over the same period a year ago.
Farmland's net income for the period March 1 to May 31 rose to $59.6 million from $48.8 million a year ago.
The company attributed the $10.8 million increase to improvements in its petroleum and crop production businesses.

Despite the increase in net income, Farmland's sales for the quarter fell 9.3 percent compared with the year-ago period. The company blamed the sales decline on a decrease in grain sales due in part to the poor 1996 wheat harvest.

"The decline in grain sales was expected based on last year's crop -- there was simply less wheat traded this year. Despite the early spring freeze, however, the 1997 wheat harvest is stronger than expected prior to the freeze," Farmland President and CEO Harry Cleberg said in a statement.
The company said expansion and improvements at its petroleum refinery in Coffeyville, Kan., resulted in higher earnings during the third quarter.

The company also said favorable spring weather conditions during the quarter allowed higher product volumes in the crop production business, offsetting lower margins in product made with natural gas bought at higher prices during the second quarter.
In 1996, Farmland reported sales of $9.8 billion.
